The Love that the Sahabah (RA) had for Rasulullaah ﷺ
The Love that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) had for Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that (during the Battle of Badr) Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) said, "O Nabi of Allaah ﷺ! Should we not build you a structure for shade so that you could stay there and your conveyance could stay in readiness with you. We shall then fight the enemy and if Allaah grants us honour and victory over them, it would be what we want. However, if the contrary occurs, you could mount your conveyance and join up with those who have remained behind (in Madinah). Many people have remained behind who love you no less than we do and who would have never stayed behind had they known that we were going to fight a battle. Allaah shall then use them to protect you because they are your well wishers and will fight by your side." Rasulullaah ﷺ praised this gesture of Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) and prayed for him. The structure was then erected for Rasulullaah ﷺ.[^2]
The Incident of the Love a Sahabi (RA) Expressed for Rasulullaah ﷺ and the verse Revealed in this Regard

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I love you more than my own self and more than my children. When I am in my house and think of you, I have no peace until I come to see you. Now that I think of my death and yours, I realise that you will be elevated amongst those occupying the highest positions in Jannah and I fear that I will never get to see you when I get to Jannah. Rasulullaah ﷺ gave no reply until Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) came with the revelation of the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَنْ يُّطِعِ اللّٰهَ وَالرَّسُوْلَ فَاُولٰٓئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِيْنَ اَنْعَمَ اللّٰهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنَ النَّبِيّٖنَ وَالصِّدِّيْقِيْنَ وَالشُّهَدَآءِ وَالصّٰلِحِيْنَ وَحَسُنَ اُولٰٓئِكَ رَفِيْقًا
blocks.text: Those who obey Allaah and the Rasool ﷺ will be (in the Aakhirah) with those Ambiyaa (those who received divine revelation),
In the Chapter about the Ansaar and under the heading "How the Ansaar Severed the Ties they had During the Period of Ignorance to Strengthen the Ties of Islaam".
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.3 Pg.268).
